name: banking_vs_it_rotation_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: BANK NIFTY and NIFTY IT are the two largest sector indices by weight in NIFTY 50 and exhibit a well-documented negative intraday correlation driven by opposing macro sensitivities: banking benefits from rate cuts and domestic growth (INR strength), while IT benefits from INR weakness and global tech demand. When one sector significantly outperforms the other intraday (>30 bps spread), mean reversion occurs as institutional portfolio rebalancers adjust exposure. This inefficiency persists because: (1) the correlation regime shifts (sometimes positive, sometimes negative) making static pairs trading unreliable, (2) the reversion time is variable (30 min to 2 hours), and (3) retail traders treat banking and IT as independent, not as a rotation pair.
universe: BANK NIFTY constituents + NIFTY IT constituents
stock_filter: Top 3 by weight: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, SBI (banking) + TCS, Infosys, HCL Tech (IT)

conditions: spread_zscore < -2.0 (IT outperforming, banking lagging — expect banking catch-up)
USDINR_direction <= 0 (INR not weakening further — supports banking recovery)
long.confirmation: spread_zscore starts rising (crosses above -1.8 from below -2.0)

conditions: spread_zscore > 2.0 (banking outperforming, IT lagging — expect IT catch-up)
USDINR_direction >= 0 (INR not strengthening further — supports IT recovery)
short.confirmation: spread_zscore starts falling (crosses below 1.8 from above 2.0)

entry.entry_price: market order: long banking proxy + short IT proxy (or vice versa)

exit.target: spread_zscore reverts to 0 (spread mean reversion complete)
exit.stop_loss: spread_zscore extends to ±3.0 (spread widening, stop out)
exit.time_stop: exit after 90 bars if spread hasn't reverted

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; in high VIX, both sectors sell off together (positive correlation)
filters.time_filter: wait until 10:00 for stable intraday spread; stop new entries after 14:00
filters.volume_filter: both sector indices trading at > 0.7x normal volume participation
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 is moving > 1% intraday (macro dominating, rotation suppressed)
filters.spread_filter: individual stock spreads < 5 bps for all 6 proxy stocks
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy days (banking directional), IT result days (IT directional)
other_filters: skip if correlation_regime > 0.3 (sectors moving together, not rotating)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — the opposing macro sensitivities of banking (domestic rates) and IT (FX, global tech) are structural and unlikely to change. Rotation dynamics persist as long as both sectors have significant NIFTY weight.

weaknesses: The correlation regime between banking and IT is unstable — in risk-off events, both sectors sell off together and the rotation trade gets stopped out.
Using individual stocks as sector proxies introduces stock-specific risk (e.g., HDFC Bank result surprise moves the banking leg without sector-wide implication).
Very low trade frequency (1-2/day) means the strategy cannot stand alone and must be part of a portfolio of strategies.
prior_art: Granger & Morgenstern (1970) early work on spectral analysis of market relationships. Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) pairs trading framework. In India, Srivastava (2019) studies BANK NIFTY-IT NIFTY dynamics. The USDINR linkage is documented in CCIL reports.
notes: Alternative implementation: trade BANK NIFTY futures vs NIFTY IT futures directly. This eliminates stock-specific risk but introduces basis risk and requires higher margin. The USDINR filter is critical — when INR is in a strong one-directional trend, the rotation dynamic breaks down.
